name: HUSIC, the Hon. Edham (Ed) Nurredin

headline.note: The frozen biography supplies a near-continuous employment sequence, but not exact dates, hours, leave or substantive full-time status. Integral Energy was NSW government-controlled during Husic's tenure, while Burson-Marsteller was private; political staff, union work, party activity, study and elected office are excluded under the codebook. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional profile Education section specifies1988–1990 at Western Sydney University; official and member biographies confirm BA(Applied Communications). Calendar-year precision only; exact enrolment/completion days and study load remain unknown. Year sequence precedes recorded1991 adviser work but does not establish absence of other paid work.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract provides the employer, role and year boundaries. Contemporary organisational history identifies Integral Energy as a NSW state-owned energy corporation during this period; the retail/network restructuring occurred later. Exact appointment and departure dates, hours, leave and any continuing union office are unresolved. Classified public_corporation to distinguish state-owned enterprise from departmental service. SBS describes media relations duties; 2003 secondary end conflicts with official 2004, retained pending personnel/annual-report evidence.
career_spells.counting_note: Government-controlled employment is supported, but full-time status and exact boundaries are not established.

career_spells.employer: Communications, Electrical and Plumbing Union — Communications Division
career_spells.evidence_note: Frozen paired leadership entry is separated into divisional and national offices. Contemporary regulatory filings give Divisional Secretary appointment 24 July 2006 and resignation 7 September 2010. This office overlapped House service beginning 21 August 2010; no assumption that paid work continued for all of that overlap. Hours, remuneration and leave remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Union employment and office are excluded from the narrow public/private headline.

career_spells.evidence_note: Frozen extract gives 2006 start. National Council 2011 report records resignation in August 2010, annotated TBA; precise day and appointment date unresolved. research_notes: The frozen official sequence is preserved even where secondary dates differ, notably the 1996–1999 CEPU role and 1999–2004 Integral Energy role.
Integral Energy is treated as government-controlled at the time; later retail sale and network rebranding do not retroactively change employer control.
The unexplained 2004–2005 transition is retained as an evidence gap rather than silently filled by candidacy or party activity.
Union and political-staff employment are excluded from the narrow headline even though they were likely paid roles.

2026-10-01 systematic follow-up: original CEPU regulatory annual/financial reports resolve divisional office dates, distinguish national presidency and reveal APSS governance. NSW 2005 committee minutes resolve minister identity. None proves full-time hours.

Searched Integral historical annual-report and Burson-Marsteller hours leads, union filings, university/alumni and interview profiles. No individual payroll/hours or Integral 2003/2004 departure reconciliation found. APH live open returned Internal Error; frozen extract preserved and independent primary filings used. Public professional/profile results added no hour evidence. Retain employer reports/personnel chronology and APSS reports as next leads.

Second follow-up2October2026 resolves study years through public professional profile and adds two omitted party-secretary offices from indexed official biography. No hours inferred from leadership titles.

Targeted Integral Energy annual-report/full-time, Burson employment and APSS appointment searches did not resolve qualifying employment hours or Integral2003/2004 departure conflict. Australia Post2009–10 annual report describes Husic negotiating as CEPU president, not Australia Post employment. Reproduced Cooper v Metcher[2015]FCA6 identifies PostSuper as APSS trustee and quotes Husic union correspondence, but does not establish his individual original board appointment; retain trustee annual-report lead. Direct LinkedIn999 and APH restricted-URL reader errors are source-level gaps; public indexed text remains available.

Follow-up3October2026 tested the original APSS/PostSuper trustee appointment lead using both search services, trustee annual-report queries and the public17December2014 trustee-director factsheet mirror at https://expydoc.com/doc/4996713/trustee-director-profiles---australia-post-superannuation... . That later factsheet contains no Husic entry; its2006–2010 directorship line belongs to another director and is not attributed to him. Australia Post2008–09 report https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/auspost-anntpt-2009.pdf identifies APSS as employer-sponsored but does not identify his appointment. Existing court correspondence and union filings remain the only located person-level leads; no new dates, individual pay or hours established. Original pre2010 trustee reports remain unresolved; defer repeated generic APSS queries until a new archive or report lead emerges.

Fourth follow-up4October2026 used exact Burson-Marsteller, Integral Energy, APSS trustee and Roger Price adviser queries. Public parliamentary handbooks repeated Burson1993–1994 and Integral1999–2004; secondary sources repeated the conflicting Integral2003 end. The original union filing again supplies only the1April–7September2010 APSS observation, not appointment origin, pay or hours. No new personnel record, hours, leave or2004–2005 transition evidence surfaced; generic trustee avenues remain deferred pending an actual pre2010 report. No material change.
